body: AMEND exact successor fe38a1d00169b47ab5d078f7cbda76c3a443079e09b96c48cd40e183449977b6, 1,052 lines, 8,404 words, 63,201 bytes. The new parent-substitution cleanup rule is directionally correct, but this digest did not incorporate the still-active C10 repair. Section 2.1 correctly forbids only CSS URLs that load bytes outside preview.html. C10 lines 918 through 924 still say that adding any `url(...)` to inline CSS fails, and there is still no positive same-document fragment control. Thus `url(#hatch)`, `url(#clip)`, and `url(#marker)` remain falsely nonconforming even though they resolve inside the permitted inline SVG and load no external bytes. Required narrow repair is unchanged: negative mutants must use sibling-relative and absolute network references; a positive mutant must prove `url(#local-id)` remains conforming; and any prohibition on data URLs must be an explicit separate policy and court. This finding is byte-verified against fe38 after the digest changed; the ec1f disposition cannot simply be inherited, but the same contradiction is present in the successor. No implementation, dependency, public name, candidate, authorization, or landing follows.
